extracted.intended_audience: chemical indexers, patent searchers, database curators, and information specialists working with patent chemical indexing
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for assigning and searching Derwent Chemical Indexing (Parts M and N) codes for chemical structures, reactions, processes, and apparatus in patent documents. Covers rules for when to assign specific vs general codes, time-ranging, code applicability, treatment of tautomers, catalysts, auxiliaries, bonds broken/formed, and related search strategy notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule of thumb for carbon chain coding
rubrics_metrics.description: "When in doubt, leave it out."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creating an overly-precise chemical code search for carbon chains can eliminate relevant references. For 0- or 1-valent carbon chains, comprehensive retrieval is often achieved by searching the general length codes (M210 for 1–6 C atoms, M220 for 7–10 C atoms) rather than overly specific length codes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Always add general M210/M220 when specific M21/M22 used
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the general codes M210 or M220 is always added to the code record when a specific code from Subset M21: or M22: is assigned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: a propyl chain not multiply bonded to a heteroatom receives M210 and M213. Prior to 1981, specific codes in Subsets M21/M22 were only assigned if there were no polyvalent chains; from 1981 onward, specific codes are assigned only if chain length is specifically claimed or exemplified. For comprehensive retrieval, search M210 rather than specific chain lengths.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time-range placement for mixed chain structures
rubrics_metrics.description: If a structure contains both 0-/1-valent carbon chain and a polyvalent chain, place specific number-of-C codes with post-1981 codes and the applicable general code with pre-1981 codes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically: include the specific C-atom count code in the search statement with codes from 1981/Week 27 to present (green codes); place the general code (M210 or M220) with codes from 1972 to 1981/Week 26 (blue codes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of Set M2 codes by subheading and time
rubrics_metrics.description: Set M2 codes apply to subheadings M2, M3 and M4 from 1972 and to subheading M1 from 1981, with exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions: M232, M233 and M240 are applicable to subheading M0 from 1963 and to subheadings M1 to M4 from 1970. Always check subheading applicability when constructing searches across time ranges.

rubrics_metrics.name: M21 and M22: carbon chain length codes
rubrics_metrics.description: M21 covers number of C atoms in chains 1 to 6 (M210–M216); M22 covers number of C atoms in chains 7 to 19+ (M220–M226).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: M210 and M220 are the general (range) codes for 1–6 C and 7–10 C respectively; specific numeric codes (M211 etc.) exist for exact lengths where assigned per policy (see time-range rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: M23: carbon chain branching codes and restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: M231 straight chain; M232 secondary branching; M233 tertiary branching (plus M240 chain bonded to ring C).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules: M231 not used for methyl/ethyl since 1981; chains coded M232/M233 are not additionally coded M231; for M232/M233 none of the C atoms may be multiply bonded to a heteroatom or be ring members; the free bond must attach to an atom other than hydrogen (examples: tert-butyl alcohol and neopentyl benzene coded M233). Chains with C=C or C≡C are assigned the same M23 code as corresponding hydrogenated chains. Be cautious searching M232/M233 due to inconsistent 'punch code' assignments prior to 1972.

rubrics_metrics.name: M26/M27: chain bonded to heteroatom (C=U/C=V/C(cid:1)U etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Codes exist to indicate carbon chains bonded to various heteroatom types (C=O, C=S, C=N, O, S, N, etc.) with separate pre- and post-1981 precursor codes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tautomeric forms: assign the first applicable code; e.g., CH3-C(=O)-SH is coded as its tautomer CH3-C(=S)-OH (M261). Check precursor-code guidance for pre-1981 records.

rubrics_metrics.name: M28 and M32/M39: multiplier codes indicate multiplicity of attachments
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiplier codes indicate how many times a given subset code applies (none, once, twice, three+).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: M280 = No 0-/1-valent chains present; M281 = one or more of a set applicable once; M282 = applicable twice; M283 = applicable three times. For polyvalent chain subsets M320–M323 and attachments M391–M393 are analogous. Adjust search logic for pre-1981 punch-code consolidations (see guidance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Precautions for pre-1981 punch-code inconsistencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Several codes were represented by combined punch codes prior to 1972 or 1981; searching must account for precursor/consolidated codes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: M313 and M314 were both represented by punch code 050 prior to 1981; to find references use (M321 OR M322) with the codes introduced in 1972. Also, punch code 536 used before creation of M331/M333 may be inconsistent prior to 1981. Consult 'Code Modifications in 1981' and 'Punch codes' sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: M33/M34: straight/branched chains and valency specs
rubrics_metrics.description: Subsets exist to indicate straight vs branched chains with or without terminal groups (M331–M334) and valency specifications (M340–M349).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes: M332 not assigned to 1-C chains post-1981; chains of type Q-(CH2)n-CH=(ring C) are coded M332 not M331; in M349 definitions C1 and C2 roles and W/W' heteroatom allowances are specified. A double bond counts as two valencies, a triple bond as three.

rubrics_metrics.name: M36–M38: chain bonded to classes of atoms (V, U etc.) and optional groups
rubrics_metrics.description: Subsets indicate carbon chains bonded to atoms other than C/H/O/S/Se/Te/N (V), halogens, ring carbons, and optionally to U/C=U/C(cid:1)U groups, with separate pre-1981 precursor codes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notation semantics: 'And (U and/or C=U and/or C(cid:1)U)' means at least one option in parentheses must be present; 'And optionally ( ... )' means any/all/none may be present. V and U definitions are provided in notes (V = atom other than C,H,O,S,Se,Te,N; U = O,S,Se,Te or N).

rubrics_metrics.name: Set M4 Basic Group codes and priority assignment
rubrics_metrics.description: M41 codes categorize compounds by general structural class (M411 inorganic/miscellaneous, M412 fused ring heterocyclic, M413 mononuclear heterocyclic, M414 carbocyclic aromatic, M415 alicyclic, M416 aliphatic, M417 incomplete structure disclosed). Only one M41 code is assigned per compound according to an ordered priority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Priority: list is ordered; the first applicable code is selected (e.g., fused ring heterocycle takes precedence over aliphatic). Polymers use M423 (not M41). For inorganic salts, OR M411 with the subset code for free acid/base when searching. If M417 assigned, assign basic-group codes for all other compounds claimed or exemplified.

rubrics_metrics.name: M43: multicomponent composition coding and 'active' definition
rubrics_metrics.description: M430: Composition with no active ingredients; M431: Composition with one or more active ingredients. 'Active' is used in pharmaceutical, agricultural, or veterinary sense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subset M43 used only for pharmaceutical (Farmdoc) and agricultural (Agdoc) patents where two or more ingredients have been indexed. From 1970 forward, applicable M41/M42 codes have also been assigned to each ingredient coded.

rubrics_metrics.name: M42: natural materials, polymers, apparatus coding rules
rubrics_metrics.description: M421 antibiotic/vaccine without structure indexed; M422 vitamin without structure indexed; M423 other natural products/polymers/polypeptides; M424 apparatus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these codes for polymers, apparatus, and natural materials of unknown structure. M421 only used with subheadings M0 and M1; M423 primarily with M0/M1 but can be used with M4 for natural and polymeric dyes. M424 assigned when apparatus is the only codeable concept (e.g. syringe).

rubrics_metrics.name: M5: ring system counting and applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: M51–M54 subsets count number of fused ring heterocyclic, mononuclear heterocycle, carbocyclic aromatic, and alicyclic systems (None, One, Two, Three+).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From 1981 forward M510–M540 not assigned to aliphatic compounds (M416 implies these codes). Ring systems referred in M53 are those in Sets G1–G4; 'aromatic' is defined elsewhere (page 94). M5 codes are used with subheadings M1–M4 from 1970 and some M0 usage from 1963.

rubrics_metrics.name: M6: miscellaneous structure codes (saturated, salts, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: M620 saturated aliphatic compound; M630 metal or amine salt of an organic acid; M640 inorganic acid salt of an organic base; M650 organic acid salt of an organic base.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: M620 used for compounds with no rings and no C–C unsaturation but may contain heteroatoms. For salts, the structure of acid/base is always indexed; the counterion is indexed only if significant to the invention. If both organic acid and base are indexed, they are indexed in separate records unless multi-ligand complex.

rubrics_metrics.name: Redundancy guidance for M4/M5/M6 searches
rubrics_metrics.description: Codes in Sets M4 and M6 are closely related and, because of M4 priority rules, searching M4 and M6 codes may make M5 unnecessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show redundant codes underlined; redundant codes can be omitted from search strategies to simplify queries. Review priority implications before combining codes.

rubrics_metrics.name: M7: role-of-compound (patent type) coding and multi-subfield scheme
rubrics_metrics.description: Set M7 codes (M710–M760) specify the role of a compound in a patent (e.g., new compound, produced, used in process, apparatus, detected/removed, medium). Detection/analysis/diagnostics and removal patents may use three code subfields (Materials A/B/C or X/Y/Z).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggested formula for detection patents: Material A (M781 OR M782); add P831 for disease diagnosis or P832 for other diagnosis and Q505 for reagent; Material B use M750; Material C use M760. If process/apparatus is a major feature add N102. Pre-1981 codes were broader and sometimes added P831/P832 to all subfields — adjust searches accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: M710–M760: interpretations and historical application notes
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions: M710 New compound/intermediate; M720 Known compound is produced; M730 Compound used in synthetic process; M740 Apparatus; M750 Compound detected/removed; M760 Compound is medium for analysis/diagnosis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes: M710 normally only for new compounds but from 1979 also used when compounds disclosed but not claimed new; therefore do not rely solely on M710 for novelty searches. M720 includes purification/extraction/separation (including optical isomers). M730 usage expanded post-1981. M750 and M760 consistently applied since ~1979 and include monoclonal antibody diagnostics and important solvents respectively. M740 implies inventive feature is apparatus and reduces emphasis on chemical features.

rubrics_metrics.name: M77 complexes and salt coding rules
rubrics_metrics.description: M770 molecular complex; M771 acid addition salt; M772 onium salt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: M770 used when two+ uncharged compounds are complexed (e.g., BF3·Et2O), but not for water of hydration, metal coordinate bonds, or π-bonding to an uncharged particle (so not for metal carbonyls, ferrocene). M771/M772 indicate structure codes refer to one ion of a salt where both ions are important; normally both ions are organic. If the salt is a new compound with known component ions, also assign M710; if the salt is known assign M782 instead of M710. Assign M630 to acid subfield and M650 to base subfield as needed. Only one of M771 or M772 is assigned to all code subfields related to the salt.

rubrics_metrics.name: M78: 'Use of a compound' coding and search recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: M781 indicates use of one compound; M782 indicates use of two or more compounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: M78 codes only assigned to ingredients significant to the patent. Because users may not know how many ingredients were coded, it's recommended to search (M781 OR M782) when interested in use-of-compound patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: M8 stereochemistry importance flag
rubrics_metrics.description: M800 is assigned when stereochemistry is an important feature of the invention (introduced in 1981).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this code to capture patents where stereochemistry is a crucial inventive aspect; applicable from 1981 onward.

rubrics_metrics.name: M9: control and time-range codes
rubrics_metrics.description: Set M9 provides codes for selecting time-range subsets and other control filters (M900 Pre-1970; M901 1970–1971; M902 1972–1981/Week 26; M903 1981/Week 27–present).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional control codes: M904 indicates both Markush DARC and Chemical Codes assigned (can be used to remove DARC retrievable records); M910 indicates structure codes generated from a Derwent Registry Number; M911 flags patents with very wide disclosure which can be negated to reduce noise but use with care as relevant references may be lost.

rubrics_metrics.name: Part N coding precondition: process must be claimed and important
rubrics_metrics.description: To be coded in Part N, a chemical process must be claimed and must be an important feature of the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set N0 (general) was used pre-1981; Sets N1–N5 are the more specific replacement. Check claims and whole patent wording to determine novelty/importance of a process (see notes on scope changes in 1979 and 1981).

rubrics_metrics.name: Part N precursor codes and time-based code applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: Many Part N codes are only searchable from 1981 forward; several precursor codes (e.g., N100, N130, N160) exist and were replaced by more specific codes in 1981.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Precursor codes introduced in different years should be OR'ed with their more specific replacements in the appropriate search statement lines for the time ranges where they were in use. See 'Code Modifications in 1981' for mapping.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope expansion rules for Part N (1979 and 1981 changes)
rubrics_metrics.description: The scope of chemical reactions covered by Part N expanded in 1979 and 1981: earlier Part N codes were only used for processes producing known compounds; after 1979 and 1981 more processes (including those with novel features or novel natural materials) were coded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From 1979 processes were coded even if end products were new when the process was claimed. From 1981 onward, Part N codes were assigned to processes having novel features even if all end products are new. Determine process novelty from the entire patent wording, not just claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coding all relevant process steps and products
rubrics_metrics.description: All relevant process codes are assigned to a reaction; in multi-stage reactions, code all steps that lead to isolated products (except tautomerism).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intermediate stages are only structure-coded in Parts A–M if stated to be novel. Overcode multiple steps in one product code subfield unless intermediates are separately coded. Fermentations are excluded from multi-stage coding unless intermediate stages are specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Which compounds to structure-code for reactions
rubrics_metrics.description: Compounds involved in processes receiving Part N codes are structure-coded in Parts A–M depending on their role and novelty: starting materials, catalysts, intermediates, and final products have specific coding rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Starting materials: coded if stated to be novel; Catalysts: coded if stated to be novel or produced by a novel process (additional Q421 subfield rules apply from 1981); Intermediates: coded if novel; Final products: coded whether novel or not. See Derwent Registry assignment rules for additional constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Derwent Registry number assignment rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Since 1981, Derwent Registry numbers assigned to starting materials and isolable intermediates, auxiliaries that provide atoms to organic products, auxiliaries limiting the invention, and all catalysts (provided compounds are mentioned in claims/examples and registry numbers exist).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registry usage affects subsequent code generation/searchability (see 'Searching With Other Kinds of Codes').

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions: starting material vs auxiliary vs catalyst
rubrics_metrics.description: A starting material contributes at least one C atom to an organic product (or at least one atom to an inorganic product). Auxiliaries are substances present that are not starting materials or products (reagents, solvents, catalysts, acid scavengers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set N4 codes describe auxiliaries. Starting materials and auxiliaries stated to be novel have been fragmentation-coded in Parts A–M since 1963, excluding catalysts (special catalyst rules apply).

rubrics_metrics.name: Catalyst coding policy and Q421 subfield
rubrics_metrics.description: From 1970 forward, novel catalysts or catalysts produced by novel processes receive fragmentation codes; from 1977 catalysts are searchable via CPI Section N Manual Codes; from 1981 catalysts in claims/examples are assigned to a separate code subfield with Q421.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a catalyst is not stated to be novel and not produced by a novel process, only limited codes are assigned (applicable A/B sets, C0–C5 for inorganic elements significant to the catalyst, sets C6/C7 and Subset C81, a Basic Group code from M4, Q421 and M730 where applicable, and C8 for elements absent). Exception: alumina/aluminosilicate catalysts are not coded in A–M because they have specific CPI Section N Manual Codes.

rubrics_metrics.name: N2/N3: rules for coding bonds broken and bonds formed
rubrics_metrics.description: Bonds broken are bonds present in a starting material changed to yield new bonds in the product; bonds formed are bonds present in the product that were not present in the starting materials or auxiliaries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do NOT code: bonds broken in auxiliary compounds, bonds broken in decomposition of eliminated parts, or bonds temporarily modified but present in the final product. All bonds formed in the product are coded regardless of which reactant contributed the atoms. In multistage reactions, code bonds broken/formed for each step between isolable structures (overcode in product's code subfield unless intermediate also coded). Examples illustrate indexing choices (e.g., C–O broken = N242; C–halogen formed = N322).
